'''Gisèle Ruiz Goldstein''' is an American mathematician known for her research in [[partial differential equations]], [[operator theory]], and applications of mathematics to physics and finance. Goldstein has won multiple awards; in particular, one of her papers was given the Editors' Choice Award from the editors of ''[[Mathematische Nachrichten]]'' in 2010, and she was the University of Memphis Faudree Chair from 2011-2014. In December 2020, ''Discrete and Dynamical Systems - Series S'' created a special issue in honor of Goldstein's 60th birthday.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Preface to this Special Issue |journal=Discrete and Dynamical Systems - Series |date=December 2020 |volume=13 |issue=12 |pages=i-ii |doi=10.3934/dcdss.2020422|hdl=11586/326029 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

==Education==

Goldstein received her PhD from [[Tulane University]] in 1986. Her doctoral advisor was [[Jerome Goldstein]], and the title of her dissertation was ''Mathematical Contributions to Thomas-Fermi Theory''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gisele Ruiz Goldstein (Rieder) |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=43354 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |accessdate=6 November 2020}}</ref>
